objects.title: Treatment-arm label set
objects.paper_statement:
For each natural number \(K\), the treatment-arm set is the finite set of its \(K\) arm labels:
\[
\mathcal A_K:=\{1,\ldots,K\}.
\]

objects.title: Binary response types
objects.paper_statement:
For a fixed number \(K\) of treatment arms, let \(\mathcal A_K\) be the treatment-arm label set. The binary response-type space is
\[
\mathcal T_K := \{0,1\}^{\mathcal A_K}.
\]
Thus each \(t\in\mathcal T_K\) assigns one binary potential-outcome value \(t_a\in\{0,1\}\) to every arm \(a\in\mathcal A_K\).

objects.title: Labeled-schedule risk $\rho_n(c)$
objects.paper_statement:
The unrestricted labeled-schedule minimax risk for contrast \(c\) is
\[
\rho_n(c)=\inf_{\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A_K^n),\,\widehat\tau}\max_{z\in\mathcal T_K^n}\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\left[\left\{\widehat\tau((A_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n)-\tau_c(z)\right\}^2\right].
\]

objects.title: Response-type count vector
objects.paper_statement:
For a complete labeled schedule \(z=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathcal T_K^n\), define
\[
\operatorname{counts}(z)=\bigl(\operatorname{counts}(z)_t\bigr)_{t\in\mathcal T_K}\in\mathcal M_{n,K},
\qquad
\operatorname{counts}(z)_t=\#\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:t_i=t\}.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{counts}(z)\) is the unit-permutation orbit of \(z\).

objects.title: Notation for response-type counts
objects.paper_statement:
For a complete labeled response schedule \(z=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathcal T_K^n\) we write \(m(z)=\operatorname{counts}(z)\) for the response-type count vector of \cref{obj:synth_4}, with coordinates
\[
m_t(z)=\#\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:t_i=t\},\qquad t\in\mathcal T_K,
\]
so that \(\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_K}m_t(z)=n\). A generic element of \(\mathcal M_{n,K}\) is written \(m\), and \(m_t\) is its coordinate at \(t\).

objects.title: Orbit likelihood $P_m(x\mid r)$
objects.paper_statement:
The orbit likelihood of arm-success counts \(x\) given allocation counts \(r\) and response-type counts \(m\) is
\[
P_m(x\mid r)=\frac{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}r_a!}{n!}\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)}\prod_{t\in\mathcal T_K}\frac{m_t!}{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}h_{t,a}!}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal H(m,r,x)\) is the set of nonnegative integer tables \(h=(h_{t,a})\) with response-type margins \(m\), allocation margins \(r\), and arm-success totals \(x\).

objects.title: Finite orbit game $G_n(c)$
objects.paper_statement:
The finite response-type orbit minimax value is
\[
G_n(c)=\inf_{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal R_{n,K}),\,\delta}\max_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}}\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\pi_r\sum_{x\in\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\{0,\ldots,r_a\}}P_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-\tau_c(m)\}^2.
\]
Here \(\mathcal M_{n,K}\) is the simplex of response-type count vectors and \(\mathcal R_{n,K}\) is the simplex of allocation-count vectors.

objects.title: Design-based squared-error risk
objects.paper_statement:
For a complete labeled response schedule \(z\in\mathcal T_K^n\), an assignment design \(\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A_K^n)\), and an estimator \(\widehat\tau:(\mathcal A_K\times\{0,1\})^n\to[-L_c/2,L_c/2]\), define
\[
R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\left[\left\{\widehat\tau((A_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n)-\tau_c(z)\right\}^2\right],
\]
where \(A\sim\mathcal D\), \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=t_{i,A_i}\), and the expectation is only over the assignment randomization. If \(p=(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau)\) is a labeled procedure, write \(R_n(p;z)\) for the same quantity.

objects.title: Orbit-procedure risk
objects.paper_statement:
For a contrast $c$, an orbit procedure is a pair $q=(\pi,\delta)$ with $\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal R_{n,K})$ and $\delta(r,x)\in[-L_c/2,L_c/2]$. Its risk at response-type count vector $m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}$ is
\[
R_n(q;m)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\pi_r\sum_{x\in\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\{0,\ldots,r_a\}}P_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-\tau_c(m)\}^2.
\]
In the two-arm contrast $c=(1,-1)$, write
\[
R^{\mathrm{orb}}_{(1,-1)}(q;m)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,2}}\pi_r\sum_{x\in\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_2}\{0,\ldots,r_a\}}P_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-\tau_{(1,-1)}(m)\}^2.
\]

objects.title: Nonzero zero-sum contrast
objects.paper_statement: For \(K\ge 2\), a zero-sum contrast is a vector \(c=(c_a)_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\in\mathbb R^K\) satisfying \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a=0\). It is nonzero when \(c\neq 0\). A rational nonzero zero-sum contrast is such a vector with \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\).

objects.title: Compatible observation-success counts
objects.paper_statement: For an allocation-count vector \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\), an observed-success vector \(x=(x_a)_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\) is compatible with \(r\) when \(x_a\in\{0,\ldots,r_a\}\) for every arm \(a\). For \(m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}\), the vector \(x\) is compatible with \((m,r)\) when there exists a contingency table \(h=(h_{t,a})_{t\in\mathcal T_K,a\in\mathcal A_K}\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal T_K\times\mathcal A_K}\) such that \(\sum_a h_{t,a}=m_t\) for every \(t\), \(\sum_t h_{t,a}=r_a\) for every \(a\), and \(\sum_{t:t_a=1}h_{t,a}=x_a\) for every \(a\); equivalently, \(\mathcal H(m,r,x)\) is nonempty.

objects.title: Invariant labeled procedure
objects.paper_statement: A labeled procedure is a pair \(p=(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau)\), where \(\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A_K^n)\) is an assignment law and \(\widehat\tau:(\mathcal A_K\times\{0,1\})^n\to[-L_c/2,L_c/2]\) is an estimator. For \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n\), define \((\sigma A)_i=A_{\sigma^{-1}(i)}\), \((\sigma z)_i=z_{\sigma^{-1}(i)}\), and \(\sigma((A_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n)=((A_{\sigma^{-1}(i)},Y_{\sigma^{-1}(i)}^{\mathrm{obs}}))_{i=1}^n\). The procedure \(p\) is invariant when, for every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n\), the law of \(\sigma A\) under \(\mathcal D\) equals \(\mathcal D\) and \(\widehat\tau(\sigma o)=\widehat\tau(o)\) for every observed-data vector \(o\in(\mathcal A_K\times\{0,1\})^n\).

objects.title: Exact orbit game reduction
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(K\ge 2\), and a nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\) in the labeled-schedule and finite-orbit games of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game,obj:def:finite-orbit-game}. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lossless symmetrization.)} For every labeled procedure \(p\), there are an invariant labeled procedure \(\bar p\) and an orbit procedure \(q\) such that \(\bar p\) is the common-unit-permutation average of \(p\), and for every complete labeled schedule \(z\in\mathcal T_K^n\),
\[
R_n(\bar p;z)
\le
\frac{1}{|\mathfrak S_n|}
\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n} R_n(p;\sigma z).
\]
The orbit procedure \(q\) is dominated by this averaged invariant representative in the corresponding orbit risk.
\item \textbf{(Exact invariant correspondence.)} Invariant labeled procedures are in bijection with orbit procedures \((\pi,\delta)\). Under this bijection, each invariant labeled procedure and its orbit representative realize the same allocation-count and observation-count rule, and for every \(z\in\mathcal T_K^n\),
\[
R_n(q;\operatorname{counts}(z))=R_n(\bar p;z).
\]
\item \textbf{(Target preservation.)} If \(m=\operatorname{counts}(z)\), with \(m_t=\#\{i:t_i=t\}\), then
\[
\tau_c(z)
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_i\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a\,t_{i,a}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_t m_t\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a\,t_a
=
\tau_c(m).
\]
\item \textbf{(Value equality.)} The unrestricted labeled-schedule minimax risk equals the finite response-type orbit minimax value:
\[
\rho_n(c)=G_n(c).
\]
\item \textbf{(Orbit saddle point.)} There exist an orbit procedure \(q^\star\) and a prior \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal M_{n,K}\) such that, for every response-count vector \(m\) and every orbit procedure \(q\),
\[
R_n(q^\star;m)\le G_n(c)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
G_n(c)\le \mathbb E_{\nu}\!\left[R_n(q;m)\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Hull bounded-schedule domain and risk
objects.paper_statement:
For bounds \(L<U\), let \(\mathcal Y^{\mathrm{Hull}}_{n,L,U}\) be the set of two-arm bounded potential-outcome schedules
\[
Y=\bigl(Y_i(1),Y_i(2)\bigr)_{i=1}^n
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
Y_i(a)\in[L,U]
\]
for every unit \(i\) and arm \(a\in\{1,2\}\). For a design \(\mathcal D\), estimator \(\widehat\tau\), and schedule \(Y\in\mathcal Y^{\mathrm{Hull}}_{n,L,U}\), define the Hull squared-error risk
\[
R_{\mathrm{Hull}}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;Y)
=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\left[\left\{\widehat\tau((A_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n)-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)\bigr)\right\}^2\right],
\]
where \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(A_i)\) and the expectation is over assignment from \(\mathcal D\).

objects.title: Two-arm specialization and the fixed-$K$ orbit game
objects.paper_statement:
Throughout, \(\rho_n(c)\) is the labeled-schedule minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game} and \(G_n(c)\) the finite orbit-game value of \cref{obj:def:finite-orbit-game}.
The following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Two-arm orbit value.)} For every \(n>0\), with \(c=(1,-1)\),
\[
\rho_n(c)=G_n(c)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
C_0(c)=1 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Two-arm target.)} For every \(n>0\) and every \(m\in\mathcal M_{n,2}\), with \(p_+(m)=m_{(1,0)}\) and \(p_-(m)=m_{(0,1)}\),
\[
\tau_c(m)=\frac{p_+(m)-p_-(m)}{n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Four two-arm response types and likelihood.)} For every \(n\), every \(m\in\mathcal M_{n,2}\), every \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,2}\), and every compatible observed-success vector \(x\), let
\[
t_{00}(a)=0,\qquad
t_{01}= (0,1),\qquad
t_{10}= (1,0),\qquad
t_{11}(a)=1 .
\]
These four response types are pairwise distinct and exhaust \(\mathcal T_2\). Moreover, with the likelihood notation of \cref{obj:def:orbit-likelihood},
\[
P_m(x\mid r)
=
\frac{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_2} r_a!}{n!}
\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)}
\prod_{t\in\mathcal T_2}
\frac{m_t!}{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_2} h_{t,a}!}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Two-arm second-order scale.)} For every \(n\ge 8\),
\[
d_n(c)\le 43\, n^{-4/3}.
\]
There are constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\kappa n^{-4/3}\le d_n(c).
\]
\item \textbf{(Exact multiarm orbit game.)} For every \(K\ge 3\), every \(n\), and every contrast \(c\),
\[
\rho_n(c)=G_n(c)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
|\mathcal T_K|=2^K .
\]
\item \textbf{(Hull risk-value inclusion.)} For every \(N,L,U\), every finite design \(\mathcal D\) on two-arm assignments, and every measurable Hull estimator \(\widehat\tau\),
\[
\sup_{Y} R_{\mathrm{Hull}}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;Y)
\in
\left\{
v:\exists\,\mathcal D',\widehat\tau'\ \text{with \(\widehat\tau'\) measurable and }\
v=\sup_Y R_{\mathrm{Hull}}(\mathcal D',\widehat\tau';Y)
\right\},
\]
where the suprema range over Hull schedules with parameters \(N,L,U\).
\item \textbf{(Strict treatment-domain separation.)} For every \(K\ge 3\), every \(n>0\), and every \(L<U\), the Hull bounded-schedule domain with parameters \(n,L,U\) is not a subset of the binary \(K\)-arm schedule domain:
\[
\mathcal Y^{\mathrm{Hull}}_{n,L,U}\nsubseteq \mathcal T_K^n .
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: First-order rule $\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cHT}}^\star$
objects.paper_statement:
Let
\[
S_c=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:c_a\ne 0\},\qquad
L_c=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a|,\qquad
q_a^\star=\frac{|c_a|}{L_c}\quad(a\in S_c).
\]
Assign each \(A_i\) independently on \(S_c\) with \(\Pr(A_i=a)=q_a^\star\). The projected contrast-weighted Horvitz--Thompson rule is
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cHT}}^\star
=
\operatorname{proj}_{[-L_c/2,L_c/2]}\!\left[
n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in S_c}
c_a\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\frac{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2}{q_a^\star}
\right].
\]

objects.title: Contrast-weighted independent design
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(S_c=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:c_a\ne0\}\), \(L_c=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a|\), and
\[
q_a^\star=\begin{cases}|c_a|/L_c,&a\in S_c,\\ 0,&a\notin S_c.\end{cases}
\]
The design \(\mathcal D^\star\) is the product assignment law under which \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) are independent and \(\Pr_{\mathcal D^\star}(A_i=a)=q_a^\star\) for every unit \(i\) and arm \(a\).

objects.title: First-order minimax constant and attaining procedure
objects.paper_statement:
Fix a natural number \(K\) and a nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\) on the treatment-arm set \(\mathcal A_K\), in the labeled-schedule game of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}. Let \(L_c\), \(q_a^\star\), and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cHT}}^\star\) be the contrast norm, contrast-weighted assignment probabilities, and projected contrast-weighted Horvitz--Thompson rule from \cref{obj:def:first-order-procedure}, and set
\[
C_0(c)=\frac{L_c^2}{4}.
\]
Then the unrestricted labeled-schedule minimax risk satisfies
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n\,\rho_n(c)=C_0(c).
\]
Moreover, for every \(n\ge 1\), the independent contrast-weighted design together with \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cHT}}^\star\) attains the finite-sample worst-case bound
\[
\max_{z\in\mathcal T_K^n}
R_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cHT}}^\star;z)
\le
\frac{C_0(c)}{n}.
\]

objects.title: Embedded two-arm converse
objects.paper_statement:
Fix integers \(K\) and \(n\), and a contrast \(c\) on \(\mathcal A_K\), with labeled-schedule minimax risk \(\rho_n(c)\) as in \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arm count.)} \(K\geq 2\).
\item \textbf{(Population size.)} \(n\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Contrast.)} \(c\) is nonzero and zero-sum.
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
C_0(c)=\frac{L_c^2}{4},
\qquad
\rho_{n,2}=\rho_n((1,-1)),
\qquad
d_n(c)=\frac{C_0(c)}{n}-\rho_n(c),
\]
where \(\rho_{n,2}\) is the unrestricted two-arm minimax risk at population size \(n\). Then
\[
C_0(c)\rho_{n,2}\leq \rho_n(c)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\rho_n(c)\leq \frac{C_0(c)}{n}.
\]
Moreover, if \(n\geq 8\), then
\[
0\leq d_n(c),
\qquad
d_n(c)\leq C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\rho_{n,2}\},
\qquad
d_n(c)\leq 43\,C_0(c)n^{-4/3}.
\]
Finally, writing \(S_c=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:c_a\neq 0\}\) for the active support, if \(|S_c|=2\), then
\[
\rho_n(c)=C_0(c)\rho_{n,2}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
d_n(c)=C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\rho_{n,2}\}.
\]

objects.title: Regular variation of a normalizer
objects.paper_statement: A positive sequence \((a_n)_{n\ge1}\) is regularly varying with index \(\beta\) when, for every \(x>0\), \[ \frac{a_{\lfloor xn\rfloor}}{a_n}\longrightarrow x^\beta \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty . \]

objects.title: Clipped-shrinkage estimator
objects.paper_statement:
Put \(h_c=L_c/2\), and let
\[
\lambda_c
=
\min\left\{
\frac{\left|\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a t_a\right|}{h_c}
:
t\in\mathcal T_K,\
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a t_a\neq 0
\right\}
\]
be the smallest nonzero normalized response-type contrast magnitude. Under \(\mathcal D^\star\) of \cref{obj:synth_5}, define
\[
W_i=\sum_{a\in S_c}\frac{c_a\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{q_a^\star}\left(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\frac12\right),
\qquad
V_i=\frac{W_i}{h_c},
\qquad
X_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nV_i.
\]
For
\[
b_n=n^{-1/3},\qquad
\varepsilon_n=\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_c}}4n^{-1/3},\qquad
g_n(x)=\max\{-b_n,\min(x,b_n)\},
\]
define the clipped-shrinkage rule
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}}
=\operatorname{proj}_{[-h_c,h_c]}\bigl(h_c\{X_n-\varepsilon_ng_n(X_n)\}\bigr).
\]
The projection is never active for \(n\ge1\), because \(|X_n|\le1\), \(0\le b_n\le1\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le1/4\); it is written explicitly only so that the rule takes values in the target interval by construction. This estimator is evaluated as a function of the realized assignment and observed outcomes.

objects.title: Universal second-order rate
objects.paper_statement:
For every fixed \(K\geq 2\) and every nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\), let \(\lambda_c\), the smallest nonzero normalized response-type contrast magnitude, be
\[
\lambda_c
=
\min\left\{
\frac{\left|\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a t_a\right|}{L_c/2}
:
t\in\mathcal T_K,\ 
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a t_a\neq 0
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
C_0(c)=\frac{L_c^2}{4},
\qquad
A_c=\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_c}}{2}-\frac{\lambda_c}{16},
\qquad
B_c=\frac{7\lambda_c}{16},
\qquad
\kappa_c=\frac{1}{2}\min\{A_c,B_c\},
\]
and
\[
d_n(c)=\frac{C_0(c)}{n}-\rho_n(c),
\qquad
s_n=n^{4/3}.
\]
The following assertions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Spacing.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0<\lambda_c\leq 1,
\qquad
0<\kappa_c.
\]

\item \textbf{(First-order envelope.)} For every \(n\),
\[
\rho_n(c)\leq \frac{C_0(c)}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Uniform shrinkage bound.)} There is a finite integer \(N_c\) such that, for every integer \(m\geq N_c\),
\[
4\sqrt{\lambda_c}\,m\exp\{-m^{1/3}/8\}
\leq
\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_c}}{2}-\frac{\lambda_c}{16},
\]
and, for every \(n\geq N_c\), the explicit clipped-shrinkage procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}}\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{z\in\mathcal T_K^n}
R_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
\leq
C_0(c)\left\{n^{-1}-\kappa_c n^{-4/3}\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Second-order envelope.)} The normalized second-order improvement satisfies
\[
C_0(c)\kappa_c
\leq
\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^{4/3}d_n(c)
\leq
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{4/3}d_n(c)
\leq
43C_0(c).
\]

\item \textbf{(Regular-variation index.)} For every positive sequence \(a_n\), every \(\beta\), and every \(C>0\), if \(a_n\) is regularly varying with index \(\beta\) and
\[
a_n d_n(c)\to C,
\]
then \(\beta=4/3\).
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Coarse two-arm lower bound
Three-arm LP value $\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger$
objects.paper_statement:
For \(K=3\), \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/2,-1/2)\), and
\[
\Gamma_M=\{-1+j/M:0\le j\le 2M\},
\]
the three-arm rational grid-action LP value \(\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger\) is the minimum of \(u\) over rational variables \(\pi_r\ge 0\) and \(w_{r,x,g}\ge 0\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi_r=1,
\]
\[
\sum_{g\in\Gamma_M}w_{r,x,g}=\pi_r
\quad
\text{for every } r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}
\text{ and } x\in\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_3}\{0,\ldots,r_a\},
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r,x,g}P_m(x\mid r)w_{r,x,g}\{g-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\}^2\le u
\quad
\text{for every } m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}.
\]

objects.title: Rational grid-action value \(\Lambda_{n,M}(c)\)
objects.paper_statement:
For \(K\geq 2\), \(n,M\geq 1\), and a rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\), define the rational contrast grid-action value \(\Lambda_{n,M}(c)\) as the optimal value of the following finite linear program. Let
\[
h_c=L_c/2,
\qquad
\Gamma_{M,c}=\{-h_c+jh_c/M:j=0,\ldots,2M\}.
\]
The program minimizes \(u\) over variables \(\pi_r\geq0\) and \(w_{r,x,g}\geq0\), subject to
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\pi_r=1,
\]
\[
\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}}w_{r,x,g}=\pi_r
\quad\text{for every }(r,x),
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\sum_x\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}}
P_m(x\mid r)w_{r,x,g}\{g-\tau_c(m)\}^2\leq u
\quad\text{for every }m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}.
\]

objects.title: Dual objective for the grid linear program
objects.paper_statement:
For the grid-action linear program with primal constraints written in standard form \(A\xi\le b\) and objective \(u\), let \(y\) denote the nonnegative vector of dual row multipliers satisfying the stationarity equations for the variables \((u,\pi,w)\). Define
\[
\operatorname{obj}_{\mathrm{dual}}(y)=-\sum_i y_i b_i.
\]
In the grid program, the restriction of \(y\) to the response-count risk rows is the response-count multiplier \(\nu\), and dual feasibility gives a lower certificate for the corresponding primal epigraph value.

objects.title: Three-arm LP certificate
objects.paper_statement:
For the three-arm diagnostic contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/2,-1/2)\) and every pair of positive integers \(n\) and \(M\), let \(\rho_n^\dagger\) be the unrestricted three-arm minimax risk and let \(\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger\) be the three-arm rational grid-action LP value from \cref{obj:def:k3-rational-lp}. Then
\[
\rho_n^\dagger
\le
\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger
\le
\rho_n^\dagger+\frac{2}{M}+\frac{1}{M^2},
\qquad
0\le \Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger\le 1 .
\]
At the resolution \(M=n^2\), there exist a rational allocation mass \(\pi\) on allocation-count vectors, a joint design-action mass \(w\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), and rational response-count multipliers \(\nu\) on count vectors \(m:\mathcal T_3\to\{0,\ldots,n\}\) with \(\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_3}m_t=n\), such that there are a rational grid weight \(w^{\mathbb Q}\) and dual multipliers \(y\) satisfying
\[
w=w^{\mathbb Q}\ \text{after real embedding},\qquad
(\pi,w^{\mathbb Q},u)\ \text{is primal feasible},\qquad
y\ \text{is dual feasible},\qquad
\nu=y_{\mathrm{risk}},\qquad
u=\operatorname{obj}_{\mathrm{dual}}(y),
\]
and
\[
u=\Lambda_{n,n^2}^\dagger .
\]
Moreover, every binary response type \(t\in\mathcal T_3\) is represented by some response-count vector \(m\) with total population size \(n\) and \(m_t>0\), and the grid-discretization error at the certificate scale satisfies
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty} k^{4/3}\left(\frac{2}{k^2}+\frac{1}{k^4}\right)=0 .
\]

objects.title: Orbit Bayes risk at an allocation count
objects.paper_statement:
For a response-count prior \(\nu\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,K})\), a contrast \(c\), and an allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\), define
\[
\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c}(r,\nu)
=\inf_{\delta_r}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}}\nu_m\sum_xP_m(x\mid r)\{\delta_r(x)-\tau_c(m)\}^2,
\]
where \(x\in\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\{0,\ldots,r_a\}\) and \(\delta_r(x)\in[-L_c/2,L_c/2]\). Equivalently, with
\[
D_{r,x,c}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r),
\qquad
N_{r,x,c}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r)\tau_c(m),
\]
\[
\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c}(r,\nu)
=\sum_m\nu_m\tau_c(m)^2-\sum_{x:D_{r,x,c}(\nu)>0}\frac{N_{r,x,c}(\nu)^2}{D_{r,x,c}(\nu)}.
\]

objects.title: Rational grid certificate sandwich
objects.paper_statement:
Fix natural numbers \(K,n,M\), a rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\), and suppose \(n\geq 1\) and \(M\geq 1\); here \(\rho_n(c)\) is the labeled-schedule minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}.  In the rational grid-action program of \cref{obj:def:rational-contrast-grid-lp}, there exist a rational allocation certificate \(\pi^{n,M,c}\), a joint design-action weight \(w^{n,M,c}\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count multiplier \(\nu_{n,M,c}:\mathcal M_{n,K}\to\mathbb Q\), and an invariant estimator \(\delta_{n,M,c}\) on allocation and observation counts such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact rational certificate.)}  There are rational grid weights \(w^{\mathbb Q}\) and rational dual multipliers \(y\) such that \(w^{n,M,c}\) is the real embedding of \(w^{\mathbb Q}\), the tuple \((\pi^{n,M,c},w^{\mathbb Q},u)\) is primal feasible for the grid program, \(y\) is dual feasible, \(\nu_{n,M,c}\) is the risk component of \(y\), and \(u\) is the dual objective value of \(y\).
\item \textbf{(Barycenter estimator.)}  For every allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\) and compatible observation \(x\),
\[
\delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}} g\,w_{r,x,g}^{n,M,c}/\pi_r^{n,M,c},
& \pi_r^{n,M,c}>0,\\[0.7em]
0,& \pi_r^{n,M,c}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
\item \textbf{(Optimal value.)}  The real value of \(u\) is the grid LP value:
\[
u=\Lambda_{n,M}(c).
\]
\item \textbf{(Certificate sandwich.)}  With
\[
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})
=
\inf\Bigl\{v\in\mathbb R:\exists r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\ \text{with}\ 
v=\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c}(r,\nu_{n,M,c})\Bigr\},
\]
and with \(U_{n,M}(c)\) denoting the unrestricted labeled-schedule risk of \(\delta_{n,M,c}\) under \(\pi^{n,M,c}\), the certificates satisfy
\[
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})
\leq
\rho_n(c)
\leq
U_{n,M}(c)
\leq
\Lambda_{n,M}(c)
\leq
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})+\frac{C_0(c)}{4M^2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Orbit counts.)}  The finite sets in the certificate have cardinalities
\[
|\mathcal M_{n,K}|=\binom{n+2^K-1}{2^K-1},
\qquad
|\mathcal R_{n,K}|=\binom{n+K-1}{K-1},
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}|\{x:x\text{ is compatible with }r\}|
=
\binom{n+2K-1}{2K-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Mesh-rate scaling.)}  For every positive sequence \(a_k\) and every integer sequence \(M_k\geq1\), if
\[
\frac{a_k}{M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0,
\]
then
\[
a_k\,\frac{C_0(c)}{4M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Asymptotic certificates.)}  For every positive normalizing sequence \(a_k\) and every grid-resolution sequence \(M_k\geq1\) satisfying \(a_k/M_k^2\to0\), the rational certificates at mesh \(M_k\) admit lower and upper endpoints \(B_{k}\) and \(U_{k}\) with
\[
B_k\leq \rho_k(c)\leq U_k,
\qquad
a_k\{U_k-B_k\}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(a_k d_k(c)\) has a finite limit \(\ell\), the scaled lower and upper certificate improvements both converge to that limit:
\[
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c)}{k}-U_k\right\}\longrightarrow \ell,
\qquad
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c)}{k}-B_k\right\}\longrightarrow \ell.
\]
At the second-order scale \(a_k=k^{4/3}\), the specialization \(M_k=k\) satisfies the mesh condition and yields
\[
k^{4/3}\{U_k-B_k\}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Contrast risk continuity
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(K\) and \(n\) be integers, and let \(c,c'\in\mathbb R^K\) be nonzero zero-sum treatment contrasts for the labeled-schedule game in \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}. Suppose that
\[
K\ge 2
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
n\ge 1 .
\]
Define the contrast distance
\[
\eta(c,c')
=
\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a-c'_a| .
\]
Then the unrestricted labeled-schedule minimax risk satisfies
\[
\left|\sqrt{\rho_n(c)}-\sqrt{\rho_n(c')}\right|
\le
\eta(c,c') .
\]

objects.title: Exact rational primal-dual grid certificate
objects.paper_statement:
Fix rational nonzero zero-sum $c\in\mathbb Q^K$ and integers $n,M\ge1$. An exact rational primal-dual grid certificate for the program defining $\Lambda_{n,M}(c)$ consists of rational values $(\pi_r)_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}$, rational values $(w_{r,x,g})$, a rational epigraph value $u$, and rational dual multipliers for the linear constraints, such that $\pi_r\ge0$, $w_{r,x,g}\ge0$, $\sum_r\pi_r=1$, $\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}}w_{r,x,g}=\pi_r$ for every $(r,x)$, and
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\sum_x\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}}P_m(x\mid r)w_{r,x,g}\{g-\tau_c(m)\}^2\le u
\quad\text{for every }m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}.
\]
The dual multipliers are rational, nonnegative on inequality rows, satisfy the stationarity equations for the same rational linear program, and have dual objective equal to the primal objective $u$. The common value is $\Lambda_{n,M}(c)$.

objects.title: Real contrast certificate transfer
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(K\ge 2\) and a nonzero zero-sum real contrast \(c\) on \(\mathcal A_K\).  For real contrasts \(c_1,c_2\), write
\[
\eta(c_1,c_2)=\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_1(a)-c_2(a)|,
\qquad
C_0(c_1)=\frac{L_{c_1}^2}{4}.
\]
A tuple \((B,U,R^-,R^+)\) is a transferred certificate for \((n,M,c,q)\), where \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) is zero-sum, if there exist an invariant allocation-count distribution \(\pi\), a rational grid-action weight \(w\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count prior \(\nu\), an invariant barycenter rule \(\delta\), a projected upper procedure, and a schedule prior such that the exact rational primal-dual grid certificate and barycenter identities hold for \(q,\pi,w,u,\nu,\delta\), and
\[
B=B_{n,q}(\nu),\qquad
U=U_{n,M}(q;\pi,\delta),\qquad
u=\Lambda_{n,M}(q),
\]
\[
B\le \rho_n(q)\le U\le u
\le B+\frac{C_0(q)}{4M^2},
\]
\[
R^-=\left\{\max\bigl(0,\sqrt B-\eta(c,q)\bigr)\right\}^2,
\qquad
R^+=\left(\sqrt U+\eta(c,q)\right)^2,
\]
\[
R^-\le \rho_n(c)\le R^+,
\]
and
\[
R^+-R^-\le
\frac{5C_0(q)}{4M^2}
+4\sqrt{C_0(q)}\,\eta(c,q)\,n^{-1/2}
+3\eta(c,q)^2.
\]
The projected upper procedure certifies worst-case risk at most \(R^+\), and the schedule prior certifies Bayes risk at least \(R^-\).

Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Finite-grid transfer.)} For every rational zero-sum contrast \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) and every pair of integers \(n,M\ge 1\), there exist \(B,U,R^-,R^+\in\mathbb R\) forming a transferred certificate for \((n,M,c,q)\).

\item \textbf{(Real-contrast approximation.)} There exist rational zero-sum contrasts \(c^{(n)}\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) and real sequences \(B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+\) such that, for every arm \(a\in\mathcal A_K\),
\[
c^{(n)}(a)\longrightarrow c(a),
\]
\[
n^{5/6}\eta(c,c^{(n)})\longrightarrow 0,
\]
for every \(n\ge 1\), \((B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+)\) is a transferred certificate for \((n,n,c,c^{(n)})\), and
\[
n^{4/3}\bigl(R_n^+-R_n^-\bigr)\longrightarrow 0.
\]

\item \textbf{(Exact rational case.)} If a rational zero-sum contrast \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) embeds coefficientwise as \(c\), then for every \(n\ge 1\) there exist \(B,U,R^-,R^+\in\mathbb R\) forming a transferred certificate for \((n,n,c,q)\) and satisfying
\[
U-B\le \frac{C_0(c)}{4n^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Three-arm grid sandwich
objects.paper_statement:
For integers \(n\ge 1\) and \(M\ge 1\), in the three-arm rational grid program of \cref{obj:def:k3-rational-lp}, there exist a rational allocation certificate \(\pi^{n,M}\), a joint design--action weight \(w^{n,M}\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count multiplier \(\nu_{n,M}\), and an estimator \(\delta_{n,M}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact certificate.)} The tuple \((\pi^{n,M},w^{n,M},u,\nu_{n,M})\) is represented by a rational grid weight whose real embedding is \(w^{n,M}\), a primal feasible point of the rational grid LP, and a dual feasible point whose risk component is \(\nu_{n,M}\) and whose dual objective is \(u\).
\item \textbf{(Barycenter rule.)} For every allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}\) and compatible observation \(x\), the estimator is
\[
\delta_{n,M}(r,x)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{g\in\Gamma_M} g\,\frac{w_{r,x,g}^{n,M}}{\pi_r^{n,M}},
& \pi_r^{n,M}>0,\\[1ex]
0, & \pi_r^{n,M}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
\item \textbf{(Grid value.)} The real value of \(u\) is \(\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
B_n(\nu_{n,M})
=
\inf_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c^\dagger}(r,\nu_{n,M})
\]
and
\[
U_{n,M}
=
\sup_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi_r^{n,M}
\sum_x
P_m(x\mid r)
\{\delta_{n,M}(r,x)-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\}^2 .
\]
Then
\[
B_n(\nu_{n,M})
\le
\rho_n^\dagger
\le
U_{n,M}
\le
\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger
\le
B_n(\nu_{n,M})+\frac{1}{4M^2}.
\]
Moreover, for every positive normalizing sequence \(a_k\) and every grid-resolution sequence \(M_k\) with \(M_k\ge 1\) for all \(k\), if
\[
\frac{a_k}{M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0,
\]
then
\[
a_k\,\frac{1}{4M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
Finally, for every positive normalizing sequence \(a_k\), every grid-resolution sequence \(M_k\), every pair of real sequences \(L_k,U_k\), and every real number \(C\), if for every \(k\ge 1\),
\[
M_k\ge 1,\qquad
L_k\le \rho_k^\dagger\le U_k,\qquad
U_k-L_k\le \frac{1}{4M_k^2},
\]
and if
\[
\frac{a_k}{M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0,
\qquad
a_k d_k(c^\dagger)\longrightarrow C,
\]
then
\[
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c^\dagger)}{k}-L_k\right\}\longrightarrow C
\quad\text{and}\quad
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c^\dagger)}{k}-U_k\right\}\longrightarrow C .
\]

objects.title: Scalar score separation
objects.paper_statement:
For \(K=3\), let \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/2,-1/2)\), and let \(\mathcal D^\star\) be the independent design assigning each unit with probabilities \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\).  For any \(n\geq 1\), any schedule \(z\in\mathcal T_3^n\), and any unit \(i\), define
\[
Z_i=\operatorname{sign}(c^\dagger_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1),
\qquad
\mu_i=t_{i,1}-\frac{t_{i,2}+t_{i,3}}{2}.
\]
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Score moments.)}  For every \(n\geq 1\), every \(z\in\mathcal T_3^n\), and every unit \(i\),
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D^\star}(Z_i\mid z)=\mu_i,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_{\mathcal D^\star}(Z_i\mid z)=1-\mu_i^2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Average-score risk.)}  For every \(n\geq 1\) and every \(z\in\mathcal T_3^n\),
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D^\star}\!\left[
\left\{\frac{1}{n}\sum_i Z_i-\tau_{c^\dagger}(z)\right\}^2
\,\middle|\, z\right]
=
\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n^2}\sum_i \mu_i^2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Scalar minimax value.)}  For the scalar experiment at \(n=3\) that retains \((Z_1,Z_2,Z_3)\) and lets each \(\mu_i\) range over the five feasible values, its minimax value is
\[
V_3^Z=1-\frac{\sqrt 3}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data certificate.)}  There exists a clipped full-data estimator using the observed arm labels and outcomes under \(\mathcal D^\star\) whose worst-case risk over \(z\in\mathcal T_3^3\) is
\[
\frac{511653}{4000000}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{511653}{4000000}
<
\frac{18213}{136000}
<
1-\frac{\sqrt 3}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Scalar moment envelope.)}  For every \(n\), every real \(M\), and every feasible three-arm scalar total \(M=|\sum_i\mu_i|\), the minimum attainable value of \(\sum_i\mu_i^2\) among scalar mean vectors with \(|\sum_i\mu_i|=M\) is
\[
\begin{cases}
M/2, & M\leq n/2,\\
(3M-n)/2, & M>n/2.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{itemize}
Thus the scalar signed-score experiment has exact value \(V_3^Z\) at \(n=3\), while the full observed arm-label-and-outcome experiment under the same independent \(q^\star\) design attains the smaller certified worst-case risk displayed above.

objects.title: Exact rational grid-certificate cluster
objects.paper_statement:
Fix a rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\) and integers \(n,M\ge1\). An \emph{exact rational grid-certificate cluster} at \((n,M,c)\) consists of an exact rational primal-dual grid certificate for the grid-action program of \cref{obj:def:rational-contrast-grid-lp}, in the sense of \cref{obj:synth_12} --- rational primal weights \((\pi^{n,M,c},w^{n,M,c})\) and the rational epigraph value \(\Lambda_{n,M}(c)\) --- together with the rational nonnegative response-count multiplier
\[
\nu_{n,M,c}\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,K})
\]
read off its dual solution. Its derived objects are the barycenter estimator \(\delta_{n,M,c}\) and the upper risk certificate \(U_{n,M}(c)\), both built from \(w^{n,M,c}\), and the posterior-mean lower Bayes-risk certificate \(B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})\), built from \(\nu_{n,M,c}\).

objects.title: Contrast distance
objects.paper_statement:
For two real contrasts $c_1,c_2$ on $\mathcal A_K$, define
\[
\operatorname{dist}(c_1,c_2)=\eta(c_1,c_2)=\frac{L_{c_1-c_2}}2=\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_1(a)-c_2(a)|.
\]
Thus $\operatorname{dist}(c,c^{(n)})=\eta(c,c^{(n)})$.

objects.title: Second-order certificate frontier
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(K\in\mathbb N\) and a contrast \(c\) on \(\mathcal A_K\) as in \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arm count.)} \(2\le K\).
\item \textbf{(Active support.)} With \(S_c=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:c_a\ne0\}\), one has \(|S_c|\ge3\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
x_n(c)=n^{4/3}d_n(c),
\qquad
d_n(c)=\frac{C_0(c)}{n}-\rho_n(c).
\]
Then
\[
0<\liminf_{n\to\infty}x_n(c)
\le
\limsup_{n\to\infty}x_n(c)
\le
43C_0(c).
\]
Moreover, \(x_n(c)\) has at least one subsequential limit, and its subsequential-limit set
\[
\{a\in\mathbb R:\text{there is a strictly increasing }\phi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N
\text{ with }x_{\phi(n)}(c)\to a\}
\]
is compact.

For every positive sequence \(a_n\), every \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C>0\), if
\[
\frac{a_{\lfloor tn\rfloor}}{a_n}\to t^\beta
\quad\text{for every }t>0
\]
and
\[
a_n d_n(c)\to C,
\]
then \(\beta=4/3\).  In addition,
\[
\begin{gathered}
\exists\, a_n>0,\ \exists\, C>0
\text{ such that }
\frac{a_{\lfloor tn\rfloor}}{a_n}\to t^{4/3}
\text{ for every }t>0
\text{ and }a_n d_n(c)\to C
\\
\Longleftrightarrow
\\
x_n(c)>0\text{ eventually and }
\frac{x_{\lfloor tn\rfloor}(c)}{x_n(c)}\to1
\text{ for every }t>0 .
\end{gathered}
\]

For every rational contrast \(q\) on \(\mathcal A_K\) whose real-valued contrast is \(c\), there exist sequences \(G_n\), \(P_n\), and \(L_n\) such that \(G_n\) is an exact rational grid-certificate cluster for \(q\), and
\[
G_n-x_n(c)\to0,\qquad
P_n-G_n\to0,\qquad
L_n-G_n\to0.
\]

There also exist rational contrasts \(c^{(n)}\), certificate values \(B_n,U_n\), and endpoints \(R_n^-,R_n^+\) such that, for every arm \(a\),
\[
c_a^{(n)}\to c_a,
\]
and
\[
n^{5/6}\operatorname{dist}(c,c^{(n)})\to0.
\]
For every \(n>0\), there are an exact rational primal-dual certificate, a grid barycenter estimator, and a rational prior for \(c^{(n)}\) such that
\[
B_n=\text{the lower certificate from the prior},
\qquad
U_n=\text{the upper certificate from the grid barycenter},
\]
\[
R_n^-=
\left(\max\left\{0,\sqrt{B_n}-\operatorname{dist}(c,c^{(n)})\right\}\right)^2,
\qquad
R_n^+=
\left(\sqrt{U_n}+\operatorname{dist}(c,c^{(n)})\right)^2,
\]
and
\[
R_n^-\le \rho_n(c)\le R_n^+.
\]
The transferred normalized endpoint improvements are asymptotically coincident with \(x_n(c)\):
\[
n^{4/3}\left(\frac{C_0(c)}{n}-R_n^-\right)-x_n(c)\to0,
\qquad
n^{4/3}\left(\frac{C_0(c)}{n}-R_n^+\right)-x_n(c)\to0.
\]

Finally, for the three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/2,-1/2)\), there exists an estimator rule \(\widehat\tau\) in the \(K=3,n=3\) labeled game such that
\[
\sup_{z\in\mathcal T_3^3}
R_3(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau;z)
<
V_3^Z,
\]
where \(\mathcal D^\star\) is the product design using the \(q^\star\) allocation rule for \(c^\dagger\) and \(V_3^Z\) is the three-observation scalar sign-score minimax value.

objects.title: Sign-pair embedding and lift
objects.paper_statement: Assume \(|S_c|=2\), and write \(S_c=\{a_+,a_-\}\) with \(c_{a_+}=h_c=L_c/2\) and \(c_{a_-}=-h_c\). The sign-schedule embedding \(\iota_c:\mathcal T_2^n\to\mathcal T_K^n\) sends a two-arm schedule \(s=((s_{i,+},s_{i,-}))_{i=1}^n\) to the \(K\)-arm schedule \(z=\iota_c(s)\) with \(z_{i,a_+}=s_{i,+}\), \(z_{i,a_-}=s_{i,-}\), and fixed zero coordinates on arms outside \(\{a_+,a_-\}\). The sign-pair lift of a two-arm labeled procedure \(p_2=(\mathcal D_2,\widehat\tau_2)\) is the \(K\)-arm procedure that maps the two labels \((+, -)\) to \((a_+,a_-)\), assigns no mass to other arms, and reports \(h_c\widehat\tau_2\) after translating the observed active-arm data back to two-arm notation. Under this embedding, \(\tau_c(\iota_c(s))=h_c\tau_{(1,-1)}(s)\), and pushed-forward priors on \(\mathcal T_2^n\) become priors on \(\mathcal T_K^n\).

objects.title: Attainment and certificates
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(K\ge 2\) and a nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\) on \(\mathcal A_K\). Here \(\rho_n(c)\) is the labeled-schedule minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game} and \(G_n(c)\) the finite orbit-game value of \cref{obj:def:finite-orbit-game}.
The following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Two-active-arm value and saddle transfer.)} For every \(n\ge 1\), if \(|S_c|=2\), then
\[
\rho_n(c)=C_0(c)\rho_{n,2}.
\]
Moreover, there exist a two-arm orbit procedure \(q_2\), a prior \(\nu_2\) on \(\mathcal M_{n,2}\), a two-arm labeled procedure \(p_2\), a prior \(\mathrm{prior}_2\) on \(\mathcal T_2^n\), a \(K\)-arm labeled procedure \(p_K\), and a prior \(\mathrm{prior}_K\) on \(\mathcal T_K^n\) such that
\[
R^{\mathrm{orb}}_{(1,-1)}(q_2;m)\le G_n((1,-1))
\quad\text{for every }m\in\mathcal M_{n,2},
\]
and, for every two-arm orbit procedure \(q'_2\),
\[
G_n((1,-1))
\le
\mathbb E_{\nu_2}\!\left[R^{\mathrm{orb}}_{(1,-1)}(q'_2;m)\right].
\]
The labeled procedure \(p_2\) is the invariant labeled procedure induced by \(q_2\), and the labeled prior satisfies
\[
\mathrm{prior}_2(z)=
\frac{\nu_2(\operatorname{counts}(z))}
     {|\{z'\in\mathcal T_2^n:\operatorname{counts}(z')=\operatorname{counts}(z)\}|}.
\]
The \(K\)-arm procedure \(p_K\) is the sign-pair lift of \(p_2\) along \(c\), and \(\mathrm{prior}_K\) is the pushforward of \(\mathrm{prior}_2\) under the sign-schedule embedding. These objects satisfy
\[
R_n(p_2;z)\le \rho_{n,2}
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal T_2^n,
\]
\[
\rho_{n,2}\le
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{prior}_2}\!\left[R_n(p'_2;z)\right]
\quad\text{for every two-arm labeled procedure }p'_2,
\]
\[
R_n(p_K;z)\le \rho_n(c)
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal T_K^n,
\]
and
\[
\rho_n(c)\le
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{prior}_K}\!\left[R_n(p'_K;z)\right]
\quad\text{for every \(K\)-arm labeled procedure }p'_K.
\]

\item \textbf{(Second-order scale.)} The normalized improvement \(d_n(c)=C_0(c)/n-\rho_n(c)\) satisfies
\[
C_0(c)\kappa_c
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^{4/3}d_n(c)
\le
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{4/3}d_n(c)
\le
43C_0(c).
\]

\item \textbf{(Shrinkage attainment.)} There is an integer \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), the explicit clipped-shrinkage procedure satisfies
\[
\sup_{z\in\mathcal T_K^n}
R_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
\le
C_0(c)\left\{n^{-1}-\kappa_c n^{-4/3}\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Real-contrast transfer certificates.)} For every rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(q\), every \(n\ge 1\), and every \(M\ge 1\), there exist real numbers \(B,U,R^-,R^+\) satisfying the real-contrast transfer-certificate conditions of \cref{obj:thm:real-contrast-grid-certificate-transfer} for \((K,n,M,c,q)\). There also exist rational contrasts \(c^{(n)}\) and real sequences \(B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+\) such that
\[
c^{(n)}_a\to c_a
\quad\text{for every }a\in\mathcal A_K,
\]
\[
n^{5/6}\,\eta(c,c^{(n)})\to 0,
\]
the tuple \((B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+)\) satisfies the real-contrast transfer-certificate conditions of \cref{obj:thm:real-contrast-grid-certificate-transfer} for \((K,n,n,c,c^{(n)})\) whenever \(n\ge 1\), and
\[
n^{4/3}(R_n^+-R_n^-)\to 0.
\]
If a rational contrast \(q\) represents \(c\) exactly, then for every \(n\ge 1\) there exist real numbers \(B,U,R^-,R^+\) satisfying the same transfer-certificate conditions for \((K,n,n,c,q)\) and
\[
U-B\le \frac{C_0(c)}{4n^2}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Three-arm rational certificates.)} For every \(n\ge 1\) and \(M\ge 1\), there exist a three-arm grid allocation certificate \(\pi\), a grid weight \(w\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count prior \(\nu\), and a barycenter estimator \(\delta\) satisfying the exact primal-dual certificate and barycenter conditions of \cref{obj:thm:k3-grid-certificate-sandwich} for \(c^\dagger\). These objects satisfy
\[
B_n(\nu)\le \rho_n^\dagger\le U_{n,M}
\le B_n(\nu)+\frac{1}{4M^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Boundary-layer problem
objects.paper_statement: A natural next question is whether the exact orbit game admits a boundary-layer limit obtained by enumerating binding response-type and allocation faces, expanding the discrete risk by a vector Stein identity within each stratum, using the \(c^\dagger\) LP sequence to choose the normalizer, and passing the primal and dual games to a stratified diffusion-control or spectral value problem with face and corner compatibility conditions.

objects.title: Attainment program
objects.paper_statement: A natural direction for future work is to start from the vector of centered arm scores induced by \(q^\star\), derive an orbit-saddle posterior mean or feedback correction from the limiting value function, lift that correction to finite \(n\), and discretize the squared ground state or dual occupation measure into a least-favorable prior on response-type counts.

objects.title: Canonical two-arm scalar schedule kernel
objects.paper_statement:
For a triple $\vartheta=(p_+,p_-,r_0)$ with $p_++p_-+r_0=n$, the canonical schedule kernel $K_\vartheta$ is the probability law on complete two-arm schedules obtained by choosing uniformly an ordered partition $(P,N,R)$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with sizes $(p_+,p_-,r_0)$, assigning response type $(1,0)$ on $P$ and $(0,1)$ on $N$, and, independently for $i\in R$, drawing $H_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)$ and assigning type $(H_i,H_i)$. Equivalently,
\[
K_\vartheta(z)=\mathbf 1\{m_{(1,0)}(z)=p_+,\ m_{(0,1)}(z)=p_-,\ m_{(0,0)}(z)+m_{(1,1)}(z)=r_0\}\frac{p_+!p_-!r_0!}{n!}2^{-r_0}.
\]
For a schedule $z$ and assignment vector $A\in\mathcal A_2^n$, define the transformed observed-score vector $S(z,A)\in\{0,1\}^n$ by $S_i(z,A)=Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$ when $A_i=1$ and $S_i(z,A)=1-Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$ when $A_i=2$, and define the scalar observation
\[
X(z,A)=\sum_{i=1}^n S_i(z,A).
\]
Under $K_\vartheta$, conditionally on $\vartheta$, $X(z,A)=p_++B$ with $B\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(r_0,1/2)$, whose probability mass is
\[
\operatorname{binom}_{1/2}(r_0,k)=\binom{r_0}{k}2^{-r_0},\qquad k=0,\ldots,r_0.
\]

objects.title: Scalar two-arm lift
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(n\ge 0\), and let \(\nu\) be any probability distribution on triples
\(\vartheta=(p_+,p_-,r_0)\) of nonnegative integers with
\(p_++p_-+r_0=n\).  There exists a probability distribution \(\widetilde\nu\)
on complete two-arm schedules \(z\in\mathcal T_2^n\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Canonical mixture.)} For every schedule \(z\),
\[
\widetilde\nu(z)
=
\sum_{\vartheta}\nu_\vartheta\,K_\vartheta(z),
\]
where \(K_\vartheta\) is the canonical schedule kernel for the triple
\(\vartheta\).

\item \textbf{(Scalar kernel.)} For every triple
\(\vartheta=(p_+,p_-,r_0)\), every assignment vector
\(A\in\mathcal A_2^n\), and every \(x\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\),
\[
\sum_{z\in\mathcal T_2^n}
\mathbf 1\{X(z,A)=x\}K_\vartheta(z)
=
\sum_{k=0}^{r_0}
\mathbf 1\{x=p_+ + k\}\operatorname{binom}_{1/2}(r_0,k).
\]
Moreover, for every \(A\in\mathcal A_2^n\),
\[
\sum_{z\in\mathcal T_2^n} K_\vartheta(z)=1,
\]
and, for every binary vector \(s\) with \(\sum_i s_i=x\),
\[
\sum_{z\in\mathcal T_2^n}
\mathbf 1\{X(z,A)=x,\ S(z,A)=s\}K_\vartheta(z)
=
\frac{
\sum_{z\in\mathcal T_2^n}\mathbf 1\{X(z,A)=x\}K_\vartheta(z)
}{
\binom{n}{x}
}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Rao--Blackwell domination.)} For every assignment law
\(\mathcal D\) on \(\mathcal A_2^n\) and every estimator
\(\widehat\tau\), there is a function \(f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
\sum_{\vartheta=(p_+,p_-,r_0)}
\nu_\vartheta
\sum_{k=0}^{r_0}
\operatorname{binom}_{1/2}(r_0,k)
\left\{
f(p_+ + k)-\frac{p_+-p_-}{n}
\right\}^2
\le
\mathbb E_{\widetilde\nu}
\!\left[
R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Bayes-risk identity.)} For every assignment law
\(\mathcal D\) on \(\mathcal A_2^n\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}
\mathbb E_{\widetilde\nu}
\!\left[
R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
\right]
=
\inf_{f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R}
\sum_{\vartheta=(p_+,p_-,r_0)}
\nu_\vartheta
\sum_{k=0}^{r_0}
\operatorname{binom}_{1/2}(r_0,k)
\left\{
f(p_+ + k)-\frac{p_+-p_-}{n}
\right\}^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Bayesian information inequality
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(\Theta=(\ell,u)\) be a scalar parameter interval with \(\ell<u\), let \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable observation space, and let \(\mu\) be a \(\sigma\)-finite dominating measure.  Let \(w,dw:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), let \(p_\theta(x)\), \(dp_\theta(x)\), \(g(\theta,x)\), and \(dg(\theta,x)\) be real-valued measurable fields, and let \(T:\Omega\to\mathbb R\).  Define
\[
J(w)=\int_\ell^u
\begin{cases}
dw(\theta)^2/w(\theta),& w(\theta)>0,\\
0,& w(\theta)\le 0,
\end{cases}
\,d\theta
\]
and
\[
I(\theta)=\int
\begin{cases}
dp_\theta(x)^2/p_\theta(x),& p_\theta(x)>0,\\
0,& p_\theta(x)\le 0,
\end{cases}
\,d\mu(x).
\]
Assume the following regularity conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Prior.)}  The density \(w\) is nonnegative, satisfies \(\int_\ell^u w(\theta)\,d\theta=1\), is \(C^1\), has compact topological support contained in \((\ell,u)\), is positive on the interior of that support, and satisfies \(dw(\theta)=w'(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\).
\item \textbf{(Likelihood.)}  For every \(\theta\in(\ell,u)\), \(p_\theta(x)\ge 0\) for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), \(\int p_\theta(x)\,d\mu(x)=1\), the fields \(p_\theta\) and \(dp_\theta\) are \(\mu\)-integrable, and
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=\theta}\int p_t(x)\,d\mu(x)
=
\int dp_\theta(x)\,d\mu(x)
=
0.
\]
For \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), \(\theta\mapsto p_\theta(x)\) is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of \((\ell,u)\), and \(dp_\theta(x)=\partial_\theta p_\theta(x)\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(\theta\in(\ell,u)\).
\item \textbf{(Target.)}  For \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), \(\theta\mapsto g(\theta,x)\) is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of \((\ell,u)\), and \(dg(\theta,x)=\partial_\theta g(\theta,x)\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(\theta\in(\ell,u)\).
\item \textbf{(Pointwise derivatives.)}  For \((\theta,x)\)-almost every point under Lebesgue measure on \((\ell,u)\) times \(\mu\), the derivatives \(\partial_\theta p_\theta(x)=dp_\theta(x)\) and \(\partial_\theta g(\theta,x)=dg(\theta,x)\) exist in the ordinary pointwise sense.
\item \textbf{(Information and joint integrability.)}  The prior information \(J(w)\) is finite, \(I(\theta)\) is finite for every \(\theta\in(\ell,u)\), and
\[
0<J(w)+\int_\ell^u I(\theta)w(\theta)\,d\theta.
\]
Moreover, all joint fields entering the risk, target derivative, squared prior score, squared likelihood score, score cross-product, squared total score, derivative-balance identity, and error-score identity are integrable with respect to \(w(\theta)p_\theta(x)\,d\theta\,d\mu(x)\) on \([\ell,u]\times\Omega\).
\item \textbf{(Boundary product.)}  For \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), the map
\[
\theta\mapsto w(\theta)p_\theta(x)\{T(x)-g(\theta,x)\}
\]
is absolutely continuous on \([\ell,u]\), and its endpoint values vanish:
\[
w(\ell)p_\ell(x)\{T(x)-g(\ell,x)\}=0,
\qquad
w(u)p_u(x)\{T(x)-g(u,x)\}=0.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\int_\ell^u\int \{T(x)-g(\theta,x)\}^2 p_\theta(x)w(\theta)\,d\mu(x)\,d\theta
\ge
\frac{
\left(\int_\ell^u\int dg(\theta,x)p_\theta(x)w(\theta)\,d\mu(x)\,d\theta\right)^2
}{
J(w)+\int_\ell^u I(\theta)w(\theta)\,d\theta
}.
\]

61ff812d38afff1f.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.MultiarmSecondorderMinimaxFrontier.multiarm_strict_extension
61ff812d38afff1f.statement:
/-- [with at least three active contrast arms, the multi-arm response-schedule hull strictly contains the binary two-arm subclass while retaining the stated second-order lower witness](goal). -/
theorem multiarm_strict_extension :
    (∀ n, 0 < n →
      rhoN 2 n twoArmContrast = orbitGameValue 2 n twoArmContrast ∧
      C0 twoArmContrast = 1) ∧
    (∀ n, 0 < n → ∀ m : CountVec 2 n,
      tauCount twoArmContrast m =
        (((pPlus m : ℕ) : ℝ) - ((pMinus m : ℕ) : ℝ)) / n) ∧
    (∀ n (m : CountVec 2 n) (r : AllocVec 2 n) (x : ObsVec r),
      let t00 : RespType 2 := fun _ => false
      let t01 : RespType 2 := twoArmNegativeEffectType
      let t10 : RespType 2 := twoArmPositiveEffectType
      let t11 : RespType 2 := fun _ => true
      t00 ≠ t01 ∧ t00 ≠ t10 ∧ t00 ≠ t11 ∧
      t01 ≠ t10 ∧ t01 ≠ t11 ∧ t10 ≠ t11 ∧
      (∀ t : RespType 2, t = t00 ∨ t = t01 ∨ t = t10 ∨ t = t11) ∧
      orbitLik m r x =
        ((∏ a, ((r.1 a : ℕ).factorial : ℚ)) / (n.factorial : ℚ)) *
          ∑ h ∈ contingencyFiber m r x,
            ∏ t, (((m.1 t : ℕ).factorial : ℚ) /
              (∏ a, ((h t a : ℕ).factorial : ℚ)))) ∧
    (∀ n, 8 ≤ n →
      dN 2 twoArmContrast n ≤ 43 * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(4 / 3 : ℝ))) ∧
    (∃ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N,
      κ * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(4 / 3 : ℝ)) ≤ dN 2 twoArmContrast n) ∧
    (∀ K n (c : Contrast ℝ K), 3 ≤ K →
      rhoN K n c = orbitGameValue K n c ∧ Fintype.card (RespType K) = 2 ^ K) ∧
    (∀ N L U
      (D : Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (Assign 2 N))
      (est : HullEstimator N), IsMeasurableHullEstimator est →
      (⨆ Y : HullSchedule N L U, hullRisk D est Y) ∈
        {v : ℝ | ∃ (D' : Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (Assign 2 N))
            (est' : HullEstimator N), IsMeasurableHullEstimator est' ∧
              v = ⨆ Y : HullSchedule N L U, hullRisk D' est' Y}) ∧
    (∀ K, 3 ≤ K → ∀ n, 0 < n → ∀ L U : ℝ, L < U →
      ¬ HullBoundedScheduleDomain n L U ⊆ BinaryScheduleDomain K n)

theorem embedded_two_arm_converse (K n : ℕ) (c : Contrast ℝ K)
    (hK : AdmissibleArmCount K) (hn : 0 < n) :
    C0 c * rho2 n ≤ rhoN K n c ∧
    rhoN K n c ≤ C0 c / n ∧
    (8 ≤ n →
      0 ≤ dN K c n ∧
      dN K c n ≤ C0 c * ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ - rho2 n) ∧
      dN K c n ≤ 43 * C0 c * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(4 / 3 : ℝ))) ∧
    ((Sc c).card = 2 →
      rhoN K n c = C0 c * rho2 n ∧
      dN K c n = C0 c * ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ - rho2 n))

4cf1719735faa467.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.MultiarmSecondorderMinimaxFrontier.universal_second_order_rate
4cf1719735faa467.statement:
/-- [there are at least two treatment arms](hyp:hK), [the contrast-score shrinkage procedure improves on the first-order risk by order $n^{-4/3}$ uniformly over response schedules](goal). -/
theorem universal_second_order_rate (K : ℕ) (c : Contrast ℝ K)
    (hK : AdmissibleArmCount K) :
    0 < lambdaC c ∧ lambdaC c ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < kappaC c ∧
    MinimaxEnvelopeBound K c ∧
    (∃ N : ℕ,
      (∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m →
        4 * Real.sqrt (lambdaC c) * (m : ℝ) *
          Real.exp (-(m : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) / 8) ≤
            Real.sqrt (lambdaC c) / 2 - lambdaC c / 16) ∧
      ∀ n ≥ N,
        Causalean.Stat.worstCaseRisk
          (fun (p : Procedure K n c) (z : Schedule K n) => labeledRisk c p z)
          (shrinkageProcedure K n c) ≤
            C0 c * ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ - kappaC c * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(4 / 3 : ℝ)))) ∧
    C0 c * kappaC c ≤
      liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤
      limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤ 43 * C0 c ∧
    (∀ (a : PositiveSequence) β C,
      RegularlyVarying a β → 0 < C →
      Tendsto (fun n => a n * dN K c n) atTop (nhds C) → β = 4 / 3)

8fa9c66e83fb3659.statement:

/-- Exact rational grid-program feasibility.  In particular, there is no `u ≥ 0`
row and no false `u ≤ h_c²` feasibility clause. -/
def GridLPFeasible (K n M : ℕ) (c : RatContrast K)
    (pi : GridPi K n) (w : RationalGridWeight K n M) (u : ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∑ r, pi r = 1) ∧
  (∀ r x, ∑ g, w r x g = pi r) ∧
  (∀ r, 0 ≤ pi r) ∧
  RationalGridWeightNonnegative M w ∧
  (∀ m : CountVec K n,
    ∑ r, ∑ x, ∑ g,
      orbitLik m r x * w r x g * (gammaMC M c g - tauCountRat c m) ^ 2 ≤ u)

9cbb104992d95c1a.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.MultiarmSecondorderMinimaxFrontier.cDaggerQ
9cbb104992d95c1a.statement:
-- @realizes \Lambda_{n,M}(c)(minimum epigraph value of the rational contrast grid LP)

/-- The diagnostic three-arm contrast `(1,-1/2,-1/2)`. -/
def cDaggerQ : RatContrast 3 where
  coeff := fun i => Fin.cases 1 (Fin.cases (-1 / 2) (fun _ => -1 / 2)) i

    (K n M : ℕ) (c : RatContrast K) (hn : 0 < n) (hM : 0 < M) :
    ∃ (pi : GridPi K n) (w : GridWeight K n M) (u : ℚ)
      (nu : CountVec K n → ℚ)
      (delta : ∀ r : AllocVec K n, ObsVec r → ℝ),
      ExactGridPrimalDualCertificate c pi w u nu ∧
      IsGridBarycenter c pi w delta ∧
      (u : ℝ) = gridLPValue K n M c hn hM ∧
      lowerCertificate c nu ≤ rhoN K n (ratContrastToReal c) ∧
      rhoN K n (ratContrastToReal c) ≤ upperCertificate c pi delta ∧
      upperCertificate c pi delta ≤ gridLPValue K n M c hn hM ∧
      gridLPValue K n M c hn hM ≤
        lowerCertificate c nu + C0 (ratContrastToReal c) / (4 * M ^ 2) ∧
      Fintype.card (CountVec K n) = Nat.choose (n + 2 ^ K - 1) (2 ^ K - 1) ∧
      Fintype.card (AllocVec K n) = Nat.choose (n + K - 1) (K - 1) ∧
      (∑ r : AllocVec K n, Fintype.card (ObsVec r)) =
        Nat.choose (n + 2 * K - 1) (2 * K - 1) ∧
      (∀ (a : PositiveSequence) (Mseq : ℕ → ℕ),
        (∀ k, 0 < Mseq k) →
        Tendsto (fun k => a k / (Mseq k : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (nhds 0) →

          (4 * (Mseq k : ℝ) ^ 2))) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧

e8681cc9841b0417.label: CausalSmith.Experimentation.MultiarmSecondorderMinimaxFrontier.second_order_rate_and_certificate_frontier
e8681cc9841b0417.statement:
/-- [there are at least two treatment arms](hyp:hK), [the contrast has at least three active arms](hyp:hsupport), [the scaled second-order excess risk has a nonempty compact cluster set bounded away from zero and above by the stated constant; any convergent positive regularly varying normalization has exponent four thirds, while the exact grid-certificate identification remains an explicit open frontier](goal). -/
theorem second_order_rate_and_certificate_frontier
    (K : ℕ) (c : Contrast ℝ K) (hK : AdmissibleArmCount K)
    (hsupport : 3 ≤ (Sc c).card) :
    let _openFrontier : List String := secondOrderRateAndCertificateOpenFrontier
    0 < liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤
      limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤ 43 * C0 c ∧
    (∃ a : ℝ, ClusterValue (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) a) ∧
    IsCompact {a : ℝ | ClusterValue (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) a} ∧
    (∀ (a : PositiveSequence) β C, RegularlyVarying a β → 0 < C →
      Tendsto (fun n => a n * dN K c n) atTop (nhds C) → β = 4 / 3) ∧
    ((∃ (a : PositiveSequence) (C : ℝ),
        RegularlyVarying a (4 / 3) ∧ 0 < C ∧
        Tendsto (fun n => a n * dN K c n) atTop (nhds C)) ↔
      SlowlyVaryingEventuallyPositive
        (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n)) ∧
    (∀ (q : RatContrast K), ratContrastToReal q = c →
      ∃ grid procedure prior : ℕ → ℝ,
        RationalCertificateCluster K q grid procedure prior ∧
        AsymptoticallyCoincident grid (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) ∧
        AsymptoticallyCoincident procedure grid ∧
        AsymptoticallyCoincident prior grid) ∧
    (∃ (cq : ℕ → RatContrast K) (B U lower upper : ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ a, Tendsto (fun n => ratContrastToReal (cq n) a) atTop (nhds (c a))) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (5 / 6 : ℝ) *
        contrastDistance c (ratContrastToReal (cq n))) atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      (∀ n, 0 < n →
        ∃ (pi : GridPi K n) (w : GridWeight K n n) (u : ℚ)
          (nu : CountVec K n → ℚ)
          (delta : ∀ r : AllocVec K n, ObsVec r → ℝ),
          ExactGridPrimalDualCertificate (cq n) pi w u nu ∧
          IsGridBarycenter (cq n) pi w delta ∧
          B n = lowerCertificate (cq n) nu ∧ U n = upperCertificate (cq n) pi delta ∧
          lower n = (max 0 (Real.sqrt (B n) -
            contrastDistance c (ratContrastToReal (cq n)))) ^ 2 ∧
          upper n = (Real.sqrt (U n) +
            contrastDistance c (ratContrastToReal (cq n))) ^ 2 ∧
          lower n ≤ rhoN K n c ∧ rhoN K n c ≤ upper n) ∧
      AsymptoticallyCoincident
        (fun n => secondOrderScale n * (C0 c / n - lower n))
        (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) ∧
      AsymptoticallyCoincident
        (fun n => secondOrderScale n * (C0 c / n - upper n))
        (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n)) ∧
    (∃ fullRule : Estimator 3 3 cDagger,
      Causalean.Stat.worstCaseRisk
        (fun (p : Procedure 3 3 cDagger) (z : Schedule 3 3) => labeledRisk cDagger p z)
        (Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.prodDesign
          (fun _ : Unit 3 => qStarDesign cDagger), fullRule) <
        k3ScalarMinimaxValue 3)

/-- [there are at least two treatment arms](hyp:hK), [the orbit game attains its saddle value, the universal second-order rate is achieved, and the certified three-arm converse establishes the stated strict separation](goal). -/

    (K : ℕ) (c : Contrast ℝ K) (hK : AdmissibleArmCount K) :
    let _deliveryScope : List String := attainmentAndK3CertifiedConverseScope
    (∀ n, 0 < n → (Sc c).card = 2 →

        (nu2 : Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (CountVec 2 n))
        (p2 : Procedure 2 n twoArmContrast)
        (prior2 : Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (Schedule 2 n))
        (pK : Procedure K n c)
        (priorK : Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign (Schedule K n)),
        (∀ m, orbitRisk twoArmContrast q2 m ≤ orbitGameValue 2 n twoArmContrast) ∧
        (∀ q2', orbitGameValue 2 n twoArmContrast ≤
          nu2.E (fun m => orbitRisk twoArmContrast q2' m)) ∧
        p2 = (orbitToInvariantProcedure twoArmContrast q2).1 ∧
        (∀ z, prior2.p z = nu2.p (scheduleCounts z) /
          responseCountOrbitCard (scheduleCounts z)) ∧
        pK = liftTwoArmProcedure c p2 ∧
        priorK = prior2.map (embeddedSignSchedule c) ∧
        (∀ z, labeledRisk twoArmContrast p2 z ≤ rho2 n) ∧
        (∀ p2', rho2 n ≤ prior2.E (fun z => labeledRisk twoArmContrast p2' z)) ∧
        (∀ z, labeledRisk c pK z ≤ rhoN K n c) ∧
        (∀ pK', rhoN K n c ≤ priorK.E (fun z => labeledRisk c pK' z))) ∧
    C0 c * kappaC c ≤ liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    liminf (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤
      limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ∧
    limsup (fun n => secondOrderScale n * dN K c n) atTop ≤ 43 * C0 c ∧
    (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N,
      Causalean.Stat.worstCaseRisk
        (fun (p : Procedure K n c) (z : Schedule K n) => labeledRisk c p z)
        (shrinkageProcedure K n c) ≤
          C0 c * ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ - kappaC c * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(4 / 3 : ℝ)))) ∧
    (∀ (q : RatContrast K) (n M : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < M →
      ∃ B U Rminus Rplus : ℝ,
        RealContrastTransferCertificate K n M c q B U Rminus Rplus) ∧
    (∃ (cq : ℕ → RatContrast K) (B U Rminus Rplus : ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ a, Tendsto (fun n => ratContrastToReal (cq n) a) atTop (nhds (c a))) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (5 / 6 : ℝ) *
        contrastDistance c (ratContrastToReal (cq n))) atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      (∀ n, 0 < n →
        RealContrastTransferCertificate K n n c (cq n)
          (B n) (U n) (Rminus n) (Rplus n)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => secondOrderScale n * (Rplus n - Rminus n)) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (∀ q : RatContrast K, ratContrastToReal q = c →
      ∀ n, 0 < n →
        ∃ B U Rminus Rplus : ℝ,
          RealContrastTransferCertificate K n n c q B U Rminus Rplus ∧
          U - B ≤ C0 c / (4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) ∧
    (∀ n M, 0 < n → 0 < M →
      ∃ (pi : GridPi 3 n) (w : GridWeight 3 n M) (u : ℚ)
        (nu : CountVec 3 n → ℚ)
        (delta : ∀ r : AllocVec 3 n, ObsVec r → ℝ),
        ExactGridPrimalDualCertificate cDaggerQ pi w u nu ∧
        IsGridBarycenter cDaggerQ pi w delta ∧
        lowerCertificate cDaggerQ nu ≤ rhoNDagger n ∧
        rhoNDagger n ≤ upperCertificate cDaggerQ pi delta ∧
        upperCertificate cDaggerQ pi delta ≤
          lowerCertificate cDaggerQ nu + 1 / (4 * (M : ℝ) ^ 2))

/-- [The AC-regularity Bayesian Cramér–Rao inequality for a target `g(θ,x)`.](goal) -/
lemma bayesianInformationInequality
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (ell u : ℝ) (w dw : ℝ → ℝ) (p dp g dg : ℝ → Ω → ℝ) (T : Ω → ℝ)
    (h : BayesianInformationRegularity μ ell u w dw p dp g dg T) :
    bayesJointIntegral μ ell u w p (fun θ x => (T x - g θ x) ^ 2) ≥
      bayesJointIntegral μ ell u w p dg ^ 2 /
        (priorInformation ell u w dw +
          ∫ θ in ell..u, fisherInformation μ p dp θ * w θ)
